name: MultiPriv
intro: MultiPriv 是评估视觉语言模型个体级隐私感知与推理风险的中英双语多模态基准。论文 v3 以 36 个隐私属性和 40 个全合成个体构建九项 VQA 任务，并把模型输出分为确定性规则核验与大模型加人工确认；固定官方仓库快照仅公开了论文基准的一部分。
build_method: 法规分类, 公开源筛选与受控合成, 人工双语 VQA 设计, 规则与混合输出核验
metric: F1, IEA 精确匹配, mIoU, Accuracy, Completion Percentage, Refusal Rate
task_type: 视觉问答, 隐私感知, 个体级隐私推理
eval_feature: PPR, 九项任务, 身份关联, 双语分层风险指标, 拒答与已回答能力分离
scale: 论文：1,119 张图像、7,414 条人工双语 VQA、40 个合成个体；固定公开快照：663 张图像、30 个个体
openness_en: Partly Public (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 repository; upstream rights vary; some attribute images are link-only; the pinned snapshot omits the paper's full VQA/evaluator release)
task_type_en: Visual QA, Privacy Perception, Individual-level Privacy Reasoning
build_method_en: Legal Taxonomy, Public-source Filtering and Controlled Synthesis, Manual Bilingual VQA Design, Rule and Hybrid Output Verification
eval_feature_en: PPR Framework, Nine Tasks, Identity Linkage, Bilingual Hierarchical Risk Metrics, Refusal-separated Capability
intro_en: MultiPriv is a bilingual multimodal benchmark for measuring individual-level privacy perception and reasoning risk in vision-language models. Paper v3 builds nine VQA tasks from 36 privacy attributes and 40 fully synthetic individuals, then routes model outputs to deterministic or LLM-plus-human verification; the pinned official repository snapshot exposes only part of the reported benchmark.
scale_en: Paper: 1,119 images, 7,414 manually designed bilingual VQA pairs, 40 synthetic individuals; pinned public snapshot: 663 images, 30 profiles
metric_en: F1, IEA Exact Match, mIoU, Accuracy, Completion Percentage, Refusal Rate
drawio_review_note: Evidence lock. The redraw is anchored to arXiv:2511.16940v3, submitted 29 May 2026, at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.16940v3. The downloaded PDF SHA-256 is 509ee52ad68517eb1e639d881e08659cf285f74c8bf163f025c532bccab1c6f8. Paper locations used are the abstract and Fig. 2; Sections 3.1–3.5; Fig. 3 and Table 2; Section 4.1; and Appendices A, B, D, E, H, I, and J. The paper itself names https://github.com/CyberChangAn/MultiPriv-PII as the benchmark location. The official GitHub snapshot is pinned to commit 3fc53f39cc96c78de05e847dedcf453174994170 (2026-06-29, “Update README.md”) at https://github.com/CyberChangAn/MultiPriv-PII/tree/3fc53f39cc96c78de05e847dedcf453174994170. The official Hugging Face mirror is independently pinned to commit a364b8428c2d3de797be557e5a8a694e0c1f934b (2026-07-03, “sync with github”) at https://huggingface.co/datasets/CyberChangAn/MultiPriv/tree/a364b8428c2d3de797be557e5a8a694e0c1f934b. Both advertise CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the repository material. Construction alignment. MultiPriv defines individual-level privacy risk around visual and cross-modal identity linkage; Section 3.1 explicitly puts text-only leakage outside this paper’s threat model. Its GDPR/CCPA-grounded taxonomy has 36 fine-grained attributes in seven categories and deliberately excludes ambiguous or poorly defined categories. The attribute-level branch filters public sources and augments them with synthesis to form the paper-reported 1,119-image pool. Appendix A does not support the old diagram’s claim that all sources are cleanly licensed: it lists Apache-2.0, CC0, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC-ND, no-license sources, an All Rights Reserved source, and a custom non-commercial licence. The official README also says some attribute-level VLM images cannot be directly published and are represented by links. The individual-level branch creates 40 fully synthetic people. Each has ten images and a detailed JSON profile; the three disclosed synthesis stages create complete textual profiles, establish stable cross-record associations using names, faces, fingerprints, addresses, relationships, and travel information, then generate or edit coherent photographs, fingerprints, transaction, and travel records using Doubao and tools such as Photoshop. Appendix B says approximately 18% of attribute-level data is generated with Doubao, then separately lists 2% fingerprints, 11% identity-card images, 5% medical records, and 2% shopping records. Those listed shares sum to 20 percentage points; the paper does not reconcile that internal discrepancy, so the diagram reports the numbers without inventing a correction. Task alignment. The four perception tasks are Direct Identifier Recognition, Indirect Identifier Recognition, Privacy Information Extraction, and Privacy Region Localization. The five reasoning tasks are Single-step Cross-validation, Single-step Reasoning, Chained Reasoning, Re-identification and Linkability, and Cross-modal Association. All are VQA-style and bilingual in Chinese and English. Appendix D/Fig. 7 is specifically a chained-reasoning authoring guideline: prepare synthetic profiles, define a genuinely multi-step question, specify verifiable expected steps, execute and compare the model trajectory, then assess difficulty and coverage. It is not misrepresented as an automated generator for every task. The paper reports 1,119 images, 7,414 manually designed bilingual VQA pairs, 40 profiles, and nine tasks. Verification alignment. Appendix E’s 93%/7% split applies to evaluated model outputs, not to dataset ground-truth construction. Samples with absolute ground truth are checked by deterministic matching (93%). Semantically ambiguous extraction or chained-reasoning outputs use Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for an initial judgment followed by human review (7%); reported Cohen kappa against humans is 0.96 for information extraction, 0.92 for chained-reasoning accuracy, and 0.84 for chained-step verification. Evaluation uses the original prompts, no explicit chain-of-thought instruction, and temperature 0 across more than 50 commercial and open-source VLMs. Perception uses F1, Information Extraction Accuracy as exact match, and mIoU; reasoning uses accuracy, task-completion accuracy, and step completion percentage. Section 3.5 describes language means for F1 and IEA with mIoU shown separately, while Appendix H and the values in Table 3 include localization in the overall perception score; the graph lists the metrics and does not invent a single formula that would conceal this paper-internal wording difference. Higher scores mean greater realized privacy capability/risk under misuse. Incorrect answers and safety refusals are task failures and are not counted as successful privacy extraction or reasoning. Refusal rates are reported separately, and the paper also compares overall with answered-only accuracy to distinguish capability from alignment. Availability audit. At the pinned GitHub tree, file enumeration finds 353 public attribute-level images, 300 individual-level images across 30 profile directories, and 10 Mobile-Agent images, for 663 images total. The same snapshot does not contain the paper’s 7,414 bilingual VQA pairs or a benchmark evaluator. Its README says the dataset will be updated after ongoing work is completed. Thus the public snapshot does not reproduce the paper’s stated 1,119 images and 40 profiles, and the diagram exposes this as a dashed release boundary rather than treating the paper counts as verified repository contents. No official leaderboard was found. “Partly public” therefore reflects both the mixed upstream rights and the incomplete pinned release; the repository’s CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 cannot erase stricter or absent rights on upstream material. Formal publication evidence [site-a11w-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3107×665 (English) and 3085×665 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3105×663 and 3083×663. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
